articles.title: Flathead on the move and bream biting in Mallacoota's top lake
body: This week's East Gippsland fishing round-up says flathead are moving around Mallacoota, with paddle-tail soft plastics working along the edges of the sandy flats. The top lake is reported to be fishing exceptionally well for bream, with bass yabbies and prawns producing fish for anglers in boats and on the shore. Elsewhere in the region, bream are the main target in the rivers and salmon and gummy shark are turning up along the surf beaches.

articles.title: 167 bird species in October, a district first, and new Hooded Plover chicks
body: Mallacoota district observers recorded 167 bird species in October, well above the usual October count and only one short of 2025's 168. The Glossy Ibis was the bird of the month and a first record for the district, and the month also brought Pacific Koel, Channel-billed Cuckoo, Australian Shelduck with very young ducklings at the treatment plant, and an emu on Genoa Road. Activity included a Birdlife East Gippsland campout, a Friends of Mallacoota weeding trip to Gabo Island and a Hooded Plover banding team. One of the banded plovers, green flag "AL", hatched three chicks with its mate on 29 October.
Source: Mallacoota Weather and Wildlife, 31 October 2026, https://mallacootaweatherwildlife.blogspot.com/2026/10/october-2026-bird-report.html
